questions.question: Define the term ‘gross domestic product’ (GDP). (2 marks)
A country’s real GDP was $520bn in year 2 and $507bn in year 3. Calculate its rate of economic growth in year 3. (2 marks)
Explain two reasons why a rise in real GDP per capita may not mean that living standards have improved. (4 marks)

A consumer price index is built from four groups with weights of 30, 25, 20, 25 and price indices of 108, 104, 112, 100. Calculate the index and the rate of inflation if the base year index was 100. (4 marks)
Draw an accurately labelled aggregate demand and aggregate supply diagram to show the effect of a sharp rise in imported energy costs on the price level and real output. (4 marks)
Analyse how a rise in a country’s inflation rate relative to its trading partners affects its current account. (6 marks)
Examine the relationship between the unemployment rate, the employment rate and the economic inactivity rate as measures of the labour market. (8 marks)
Explain two causes of unemployment that would not be removed by a rise in aggregate demand. (4 marks)
Discuss the costs of unemployment to an economy. (14 marks)
Evaluate whether a persistent current account deficit should be a matter of concern for a government. (20 marks)
